## Table 1 and sensitivity with cor.type = "shrink" (run outside RStudio)

`cor.type = "shrink"` (recommended in `?anova.manyglm` when feasible; used in the Arctic
paper) weights the test statistic by a ridge-shrunk taxon correlation matrix, so blocks of
co-occurring taxa count less. It takes ~26 h per 999 bootstraps on one core here, so the
multivariate tests run in a standalone script that splits the bootstraps across cores
(`manyglm_shrink_parallel.R`, fixed seed via `bootID`, so results are reproducible).
Per-taxon tests (Fig 4) stay cor.type "I" (days with shrink).

Sensitivity: the same test on versions of the community matrix, all with the same 73
samples. Main (Table 1, decided 2026-10-27) = both primers, a taxon present only at
>= 0.1% of a sample's reads (`pa_min_pct`; detections below this reproduced poorly
between extraction replicates). Compared with: both primers with every detection, and
18S_V9 only / 18S_V7 only at the same 0.1% cutoff. Mantel r = correlation of each
version's Jaccard distances with the main version. Question: does a single primer
(cheaper) give the same statistical conclusions, even though it detects fewer taxa?
Dataset keys in the results file: "main" = all detections (historic name), "pct01" =
>= 0.1%; v9 / v7 = single primer, all detections (run 2026-10-26, not shown);
v9_pct01 / v7_pct01 = single primer, >= 0.1%.

Considered and not included (2026-10-26): log extract DNA concentration as a first term.
It correlates with richness and distance to shore, but coral has the lowest
concentration and the highest richness, so it is not a clean technical covariate.

`export_mva_inputs` saves the matrices; run it, then in the terminal
`caffeinate -ims Rscript manyglm_shrink_parallel.R` (datasets already in the results
file are skipped). `sensitivity` only reads the results.

```{r export_mva_inputs}
## all versions run by manyglm_shrink_parallel.R; sens_show = rows of the table (first
## = main = Table 1)
sens_sets <- list(
  main     = list(label = "Both primers, all detections", prims = c("18S_V9", "18S_V7"), min_pct = 0),
  pct01    = list(label = "Both primers, >= 0.1%",        prims = c("18S_V9", "18S_V7"), min_pct = 0.001),
  v9       = list(label = "18S_V9 only, all detections",  prims = "18S_V9",             min_pct = 0),
  v7       = list(label = "18S_V7 only, all detections",  prims = "18S_V7",             min_pct = 0),
  v9_pct01 = list(label = "18S_V9 only, >= 0.1%",         prims = "18S_V9",             min_pct = 0.001),
  v7_pct01 = list(label = "18S_V7 only, >= 0.1%",         prims = "18S_V7",             min_pct = 0.001)
)
sens_show <- c(tab1_set, setdiff(c("pct01", "main", "v9_pct01", "v7_pct01"), tab1_set))
sens_sets[[tab1_set]]$label <- paste(sens_sets[[tab1_set]]$label, "(main)")

## community matrices on the env_mva samples (same rows, same order)
sens_comm <- lapply(sens_sets, function(p) {
  m <- make_comm(dat_all_filt, prims = p$prims, min_pct = p$min_pct)
  m <- m[as.character(env_mva$sample_id), ]
  m[is.na(m)] <- 0L                     # sample with no taxa in this version
  m[, colSums(m) > 0]
})
stopifnot(identical(dim(sens_comm[[tab1_set]]), dim(comm_pa)))   # = Table 1 matrix

saveRDS(list(comm = sens_comm, env_mva = env_mva, date = Sys.Date()),
        paste0(dir, "manyglm_inputs.rds"))
```

## Sensitivity table (primer and presence cutoff)
Reads the shrink results; run after `export_mva_inputs` (needs `sens_comm`).
```{r sensitivity}
## Jaccard distances; Mantel against the main version
sens_dist <- lapply(sens_comm[sens_show], vegdist, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)
sens_mantel <- sapply(sens_dist, function(d) {
  mt <- mantel(sens_dist[[tab1_set]], d, permutations = 999)
  c(r = unname(mt$statistic), p = mt$signif)
})

## table: one row per version; score (p) per term from the shrink runs
sens_tab <- imap_dfr(sens_sets[sens_show], function(p, nm) {
  tb <- shrink_res$tables[[nm]]
  cell <- if (is.null(tb)) NULL else {
    tb <- tb[-1, ]                       # drop intercept row
    setNames(sprintf("%.1f (%.3f)", tb$score, tb$p), rownames(tb))
  }
  tibble(Dataset           = p$label,
         `Taxa`            = ncol(sens_comm[[nm]]),
         `Taxa per sample` = round(mean(rowSums(sens_comm[[nm]]))),
         `Mantel r`        = round(sens_mantel["r", nm], 2),
         !!!as.list(cell))
}) %>%
  rename(any_of(c(Habitat = "habitat", `SST (mean)` = "sTemp", Nitrate = "snitrate",
                  `Primary productivity (range)` = "spp_range",
                  `Distance to shore` = "sland_distance"))) %>%
  mutate(across(-c(Dataset, Taxa, `Taxa per sample`, `Mantel r`),
                ~ coalesce(., "not run yet")))

kable(sens_tab,
      caption = paste("Table S. Sensitivity of the multivariate GLM to primer choice and",
                      "presence cutoff (cor.type = 'shrink',", shrink_res$n_boot,
                      "PIT-trap bootstraps). Cells = score statistic (p-value), terms",
                      "tested sequentially; Mantel r = correlation of Jaccard distances",
                      "with the main dataset."),
      format = "html") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE, bootstrap_options = NULL)

write.csv(sens_tab, paste0(dir, export_file, "TableS_sensitivity_primer_cutoff.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
```


## Fig 4 — Multivariate GLM plot

```{r multivar_plot_ggplot, warning=FALSE}
t         <- mva_mod
t.an      <- mva_aov_uni
taxa_file <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim

## variable display order and axis labels
## Two habitat contrasts from model 1 (Coral ref) + SvM from model 2 (Mangrove ref).
var_order <- c("habitatMangrove", "habitatSeagrass", "SvM",
               "sTemp", "snitrate", "spp_range", "sland_distance")
x_labels  <- c("Mangrove vs Coral", "Seagrass vs Coral", "Seagrass vs Mangrove",
               "SST mean", "Nitrate", "Prim. prod. range", "Dist. to shore")

## p_min_val is auto-calculated below to display ~15 taxa
num_clust  <- 5            # hierarchical clusters for y-axis colour grouping
ccll       <- c(wesanderson::wes_palette("Moonrise2", n = 2), "black")  # matches Arctic
## pal3 and pal_div (dot colours) are defined in barplot_helpers

## ── Extract model 1 components ───────────────────────────────────────────────
## anova$uni.test: rows = predictors, cols = taxa — transpose to get rows = taxa
t.coef <- coef(t)
t.ts   <- t(t.an$uni.test)   # rows = taxa, cols = predictors
t.p    <- t(t.an$uni.p)

## test statistic (long format)
mult_dat <- data.frame(t.ts) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("X.Intercept.", "X.Intercept"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-lineage, names_to = "variable", values_to = "test_stat")

## p-value (long)
mult_dat_p <- data.frame(t.p) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("X.Intercept.", "X.Intercept"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-lineage, names_to = "variable", values_to = "p.value")

## coefficient (long)
mult_dat_c <- data.frame(t(t.coef)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("X.Intercept.", "X.Intercept"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-lineage, names_to = "variable", values_to = "coef")

## ── Expand combined "habitat" anova row into two named contrast rows ----------
## anova tests habitat as a 2-df term; duplicate that row so both contrasts
## appear as columns in the plot. Coefficient direction comes from coef() below.
expand_hab <- function(df) {
  hab <- df %>% filter(variable == "habitat")
  bind_rows(
    df %>% filter(variable != "habitat"),
    hab %>% mutate(variable = "habitatMangrove"),
    hab %>% mutate(variable = "habitatSeagrass")
  )
}
mult_dat   <- expand_hab(mult_dat)
mult_dat_p <- expand_hab(mult_dat_p)

## ── Add Seagrass vs Mangrove from model 2 anova ──────────────────────────────
## Tile significance: combined 2-df habitat row from mva_aov_uni2 (same test
## as MvC/SvC but from model 2). Coefficient direction: habitatSeagrass in
## model 2 = Seagrass vs Mangrove contrast (Mangrove is reference).
svM_ts <- data.frame(t(mva_aov_uni2$uni.test)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(lineage, test_stat = habitat) %>%
  mutate(variable = "SvM") %>%
  filter(lineage %in% mult_dat$lineage)

svM_p <- data.frame(t(mva_aov_uni2$uni.p)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(lineage, p.value = habitat) %>%
  mutate(variable = "SvM") %>%
  filter(lineage %in% mult_dat$lineage)

svM_c <- data.frame(t(coef(mva_mod2))) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(lineage, coef = habitatSeagrass) %>%
  mutate(variable = "SvM") %>%
  filter(lineage %in% mult_dat$lineage)

mult_dat   <- bind_rows(mult_dat,   svM_ts)
mult_dat_p <- bind_rows(mult_dat_p, svM_p)
mult_dat_c <- bind_rows(mult_dat_c, svM_c)
## ── Auto-select p_min_val to display ~n_target taxa --------------------------
n_target  <- 15
p_min_val <- mult_dat_p %>%
  group_by(lineage) %>%
  summarise(min_p = min(p.value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(min_p) %>%
  slice(min(n_target, n())) %>%
  pull(min_p)
cat("p_min_val =", round(p_min_val, 4), "| taxa displayed:", n_target, "\n")

## join; keep taxa with at least one predictor at p ≤ p_min_val
mult_dat2 <- mult_dat %>%
  left_join(mult_dat_p, by = c("lineage", "variable")) %>%
  left_join(mult_dat_c, by = c("lineage", "variable")) %>%
  group_by(lineage) %>%
  filter(any(p.value <= p_min_val)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    p_val_col = if_else(p.value <= 0.05, "significant", "not significant"),
    coef_log  = if_else(coef >= 0, log(coef + 1), -log(abs(coef) + 1))
  )

## ── Hierarchical clustering of taxa by coefficient ───────────────────────────
## Cluster on continuous predictors only — habitat dummies excluded as they
## represent contrasts vs reference level, not a continuous gradient.
cont_pred <- c("sTemp", "snitrate", "spp_range", "sland_distance")
clus <- t(t.coef)[, cont_pred, drop = FALSE]
clus <- clus[match(unique(mult_dat2$lineage), rownames(clus)), , drop = FALSE]

hc      <- hclust(sqrt(dist(clus)))
plot(hc, main = "Taxa dendrogram (coefficient distances)")
rect.hclust(hc, k = num_clust)

clgroup <- data.frame(group = cutree(hc, k = num_clust)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage")
ccc     <- data.frame(group = seq_len(num_clust),
                      color = rep(ccll, length.out = num_clust))

clustorder <- clgroup %>%
  left_join(ccc, by = "group") %>%
  mutate(taxa_cluster_arrange = as.integer(
    factor(lineage, levels = hc$labels[hc$order])
  ))

## ── Y-axis labels: Phylum;Order;Family;Genus ─────────────────────────────────
## Row names in t.p are R-safe lineage strings (;→. space→. -→.).
## Create matching 'lineage_stat' from the original lineage column to join.
rn <- data.frame(lineage_stat = rownames(t.p))

y_labels_make <- taxa_file %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(lineage:Species) %>%
  distinct(lineage, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(lineage_stat = make.names(lineage)) %>%
  inner_join(rn, by = "lineage_stat") %>%
  unite(y_labels, Phylum:Genus, sep = ";", remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(y_labels = gsub("Eukaryota", "Unclassified", y_labels),
         y_labels = gsub("NA",        "Unclassified", y_labels))

y_labels <- clustorder %>%
  left_join(y_labels_make, by = c("lineage" = "lineage_stat")) %>%
  arrange(taxa_cluster_arrange) %>%
  mutate(y_labels = if_else(is.na(y_labels), lineage, y_labels))

## ── Build plotting data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Convert variable to factor and drop rows not in var_order (e.g. combined
## 'habitat' term if anova didn't expand dummies), then derive xx/yy from
## factor integers — robust to any number of variables per taxon.
mult_dat3 <- mult_dat2 %>%
  left_join(clustorder, by = "lineage") %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = var_order)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(variable)) %>%
  arrange(taxa_cluster_arrange, variable) %>%
  mutate(
    xx = as.integer(variable),
    yy = as.integer(factor(lineage, levels = unique(lineage)))
  )

cat("Variables in plot:", paste(sort(unique(as.character(mult_dat3$variable))), collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("Taxa in plot:", n_distinct(mult_dat3$lineage), "\n")

## ── Plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
upper_coef <- 0.9
lower_coef <- -upper_coef
dd         <- 2   # divisor for intermediate legend breaks

mult_plot <- ggplot(mult_dat3, aes(xx, yy)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = p_val_col), colour = "grey50",
            width = 0.92, height = 0.92) +   # separated tiles, as in Fig 6
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_sig, limits = names(col_sig), breaks = "significant",
                    labels = "p \u2264 0.05", na.value = col_sig[["not significant"]],
                    name = NULL) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = coef_log, size = test_stat)) +
  scale_color_gradientn(
    name   = "Coefficient",
    colors = pal_div,
    space  = "Lab",
    values = scales::rescale(c(lower_coef * 1.1, lower_coef / 9, 0,
                               upper_coef / 9,   upper_coef * 1.1)),
    limits = c(lower_coef * 1.1, upper_coef * 1.1),
    breaks = c(lower_coef, lower_coef / dd, 0, upper_coef / dd, upper_coef),
    labels = round(c(-(exp(abs(lower_coef)) - 1),
                     -(exp(abs(lower_coef / dd)) - 1),
                     0,
                      (exp(upper_coef / dd) - 1),
                      (exp(upper_coef) - 1)), 1),
    oob    = scales::squish
  ) +
  scale_size(name = "Score statistic", range = c(1, 7)) +
  scale_x_continuous(name = NULL,
                     breaks = seq_along(levels(mult_dat3$variable)),
                     labels = x_labels[seq_along(levels(mult_dat3$variable))],
                     guide  = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = NULL,
                     breaks = seq_along(y_labels$y_labels),
                     labels = y_labels$y_labels,
                     expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(colour = y_labels$color),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid   = element_blank()
  )

mult_plot

ggsave(mult_plot,
       file   = paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig4_multvar_taxa_presabs.tiff"),
       width  = 20, height = 25, units = "cm", dpi = "print")
```


## NMDS and ordisurf GAMs

```{r nmds_gam}
## ---- NMDS on presence/absence (Jaccard) -------------------------------------
## Same matrix as manyglm (comm_pa), so all analyses use presence/absence; no extra
## occurrence cut (the old >= 2 samples cut was removed 2026-10-26)
comm_nmds <- comm_pa[as.character(env_mva$sample_id), ]
comm_nmds <- comm_nmds[, colSums(comm_nmds) > 0]

set.seed(20261026)   # metaMDS uses random starts
nmds_res <- metaMDS(comm_nmds,
                    distance      = "jaccard",
                    binary        = TRUE,
                    trymax        = 100,
                    autotransform = FALSE,
                    trace         = FALSE)

cat("NMDS stress:", round(nmds_res$stress, 3), "\n")
## Stress < 0.1 = good; 0.1-0.2 = fair; > 0.2 = poor

## ---- individual GAMs via ordisurf ------------------------------------------
## All continuous env variables run individually; habitat excluded (categorical,
## already in manyglm). Raw (unscaled) values used; ordisurf scales internally.
## Variables removed from manyglm due to covariance are included here to show
## non-linear gradients alongside the manyglm set.
env_vars_gam <- list(
  "Latitude"                     = env_mva$lat,
  "SST (mean)"                   = env_mva$sst_mean,
  "SST (range)"                  = env_mva$SST_range,
  "Nitrate"                      = env_mva$nitrate,
  "Primary productivity (mean)"  = env_mva$pp_mean,
  "Primary productivity (range)" = env_mva$pp_range,
  "Salinity"                     = env_mva$salinity,
  "Distance to shore"            = env_mva$land_distance
)

ordisurf_fits <- list()

tab2_raw <- lapply(names(env_vars_gam), function(v) {
  vals <- env_vars_gam[[v]]
  if (sum(!is.na(vals)) < 5) return(NULL)
  surf <- ordisurf(nmds_res, vals, plot = FALSE, bs = "tp")
  ordisurf_fits[[v]] <<- surf  # <<- needed: lapply creates child env; list lives in parent
  s  <- summary(surf)
  st <- s$s.table
  data.frame(
    variable           = v,
    Est.DF             = round(st[1, "edf"],    2),
    Ref.DF             = round(st[1, "Ref.df"], 2),
    F.value            = round(st[1, "F"],      2),
    p.value            = round(st[1, "p-value"],4),
    deviance_explained = round(s$dev.expl * 100, 1),
    stringsAsFactors   = FALSE
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()
```

```{r MDS_GAM}
## ── Species labels for NMDS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Build family-level labels prioritised by number of samples a taxon occurs in

## multivar_plot_ggplot above.
cc_name <- data.frame(lineage = colnames(comm_nmds))

y_labels_mds <- taxa_file %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(lineage:Species) %>%
  distinct(lineage, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    lineage_stat = gsub(";", ".", lineage),
    lineage_stat = gsub(" ",  ".", lineage_stat),
    lineage_stat = gsub("-",  ".", lineage_stat)
  ) %>%
  inner_join(cc_name, by = "lineage") %>%
  unite(y_labels, Phylum:Genus, sep = ";", remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(y_labels        = gsub("NA", "Unclassified", y_labels),
         Family_label    = if_else(is.na(Family) | Family == "NA", "", Family),
         priority_occ    = colSums(comm_nmds)[lineage],
         priority_occ    = if_else(is.na(Family) | Family == "NA", 0, priority_occ)) %>%
  ## same order as the NMDS species scores (orditorp matches labels by position)
  arrange(match(lineage, colnames(comm_nmds)))
stopifnot(identical(y_labels_mds$lineage, colnames(comm_nmds)))

## Site colours by habitat (env_mva row order matches nmds_res)
```

## Build L, R, Q matrices

```{r fc_matrices}
## ---- 1. Build the L matrix (sites × species, presence/absence) --------------
## Same matrix as manyglm (comm_pa). L_long (percent reads) is kept only for the
## read-coverage line in trait_diagnostics.
L_long <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(sample_id, lineage, percent_reads) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, lineage) %>%
  summarise(percent_reads = sum(percent_reads), .groups = "drop")

L_wide <- comm_pa

## ---- 2. Build the R matrix (sites × env variables) -------------------------
## Matches manyglm predictors: 4 continuous env vars + habitat (categorical).
## dudi.hillsmith() handles mixed continuous/factor variables.
## fourthcorner uses D2 statistic for continuous R × Q pairs and
## G statistic (chi-square-like) for categorical R (habitat) × Q pairs.
env_vars <- c("sst_mean", "nitrate", "pp_range", "land_distance")

env_sub <- env %>%
  rename_all(tolower) %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(L_wide)) %>%
  arrange(match(sample_id, rownames(L_wide)))

R_mat <- env_sub %>%
  select(all_of(tolower(env_vars))) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~as.numeric(scale(.)))) %>%
  as.data.frame()
rownames(R_mat) <- env_sub$sample_id

## Add habitat as categorical variable
hab_lookup   <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>% distinct(sample_id, habitat)
R_mat$habitat <- factor(
  hab_lookup$habitat[match(rownames(R_mat), hab_lookup$sample_id)]
)

L_wide <- L_wide[rownames(R_mat), ]

## ---- 3. Build the Q matrix (species × traits) ------------------------------
## Lineage prefix mismatch: L_wide uses "Eukaryota;..." but trait_dat starts at
## kingdom — strip prefix for matching, restore afterwards (same as tiding join).
lwide_stripped <- sub("^[^;]+;", "", colnames(L_wide))

## trait_dat = final trait data (one row per lineage)
## planktonic_larva left out (decided 2026-10-23): it applies only to metazoans and
## is confounded with size/kingdom (212 of 219 "yes" are animals); kept in the trait
## table for a possible metazoan-only fourth-corner analysis
fc_traits <- c("zone", "trophic_level", "size_class", "mobility")
Q_mat <- trait_dat %>%
  distinct(lineage, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(lineage %in% lwide_stripped) %>%
  select(lineage, all_of(fc_traits)) %>%
  column_to_rownames("lineage") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

## Align species: intersect on stripped names, restore full-prefix rownames.
shared_stripped <- intersect(lwide_stripped, rownames(Q_mat))
keep_cols       <- colnames(L_wide)[lwide_stripped %in% shared_stripped]
L_wide          <- L_wide[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]
rownames(Q_mat) <- keep_cols[match(rownames(Q_mat),
                                   sub("^[^;]+;", "", keep_cols))]
Q_mat           <- Q_mat[colnames(L_wide), , drop = FALSE]

## Drop species with any remaining NA trait values and re-align L_wide.
complete_sp <- rownames(Q_mat)[complete.cases(Q_mat)]
Q_mat  <- Q_mat[complete_sp, , drop = FALSE]
L_wide <- L_wide[, complete_sp, drop = FALSE]
cat("Species retained after NA filter:", nrow(Q_mat), "\n")
```


## Trait diagnostics
Run after `fc_matrices` to verify category counts before the permutation test.
```{r trait_diagnostics}
## ── 1. Species counts at each filtering step ──────────────────────────────────
n_total_sp <- length(lwide_stripped)
n_matched  <- length(shared_stripped)
n_complete <- nrow(Q_mat)

step_df <- data.frame(
  Step = c("Species in community (L_wide)",
           "Matched to trait file",
           "  Not matched (absent from trait file)",
           "Retained — complete trait data",
           "  Dropped — ≥ 1 trait value missing"),
  N    = c(n_total_sp, n_matched, n_total_sp - n_matched,
           n_complete,  n_matched  - n_complete)
)
kable(step_df, col.names = c("Step", "N species"), format = "html",
      caption = "Species retained at each filtering step for fourth-corner / RLQ") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

## ── 2. Community read coverage ────────────────────────────────────────────────
reads_total    <- sum(L_long$percent_reads[
                    L_long$sample_id %in% rownames(L_wide)])
reads_retained <- sum(L_long$percent_reads[
                    L_long$sample_id %in% rownames(L_wide) &
                    L_long$lineage %in% colnames(L_wide)])
cat(sprintf(
  "\nRead coverage: retained species account for %.1f%% of reads in analysed samples.\n\n",
  100 * reads_retained / reads_total
))

## ── 3. Missing data by trait (among matched species, before NA filter) ─────────
Q_all_matched <- trait_dat %>%
  distinct(lineage, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(lineage %in% shared_stripped) %>%
  select(all_of(fc_traits))

miss_df <- data.frame(
  Trait       = colnames(Q_all_matched),
  Present     = sapply(Q_all_matched, function(x) sum(!is.na(x))),
  Missing     = sapply(Q_all_matched, function(x) sum( is.na(x))),
  Pct_missing = round(100 * sapply(Q_all_matched, function(x) mean(is.na(x))), 1)
)
kable(miss_df, row.names = FALSE, format = "html",
      col.names = c("Trait", "Present", "Missing", "% missing"),
      caption = paste("Missing trait data among", n_matched,
                      "species matched to trait file")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

## ── 4. Category counts per trait in Q_mat (species used in analysis) ──────────
count_list <- lapply(colnames(Q_mat), function(tr) {
  col <- Q_mat[[tr]]
  if (is.factor(col)) {
    tbl <- sort(table(col), decreasing = TRUE)
    data.frame(Trait    = tr,
               Category = names(tbl),
               N        = as.integer(tbl),
               Flag     = ifelse(as.integer(tbl) < 5, "< 5 — consider merging", ""),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    data.frame(Trait    = tr,
               Category = sprintf("continuous  [%.2f – %.2f]",
                                  min(col, na.rm = TRUE), max(col, na.rm = TRUE)),
               N        = sum(!is.na(col)),
               Flag     = "",
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
})
count_df <- bind_rows(count_list)
kable(count_df, row.names = FALSE, format = "html",
      col.names = c("Trait", "Category", "N species", "Flag"),
      caption = paste("Trait category counts in Q_mat (", nrow(Q_mat),
                      "species). Yellow = < 5 species; consider merging.")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(which(count_df$Flag != ""), background = "#fff3cd")

## ── 5. Cross-tabulations of all factor trait pairs ────────────────────────────
cat("\n=== Cross-tabulations of factor trait pairs (flag cells < 3 species) ===\n\n")
factor_traits <- names(which(sapply(Q_mat, is.factor)))
if (length(factor_traits) >= 2) {
  for (pair in combn(factor_traits, 2, simplify = FALSE)) {
    ct <- table(Q_mat[[pair[1]]], Q_mat[[pair[2]]], dnn = pair)
    cat(pair[1], "×", pair[2], ":\n")
    print(ct)
    if (any(ct > 0 & ct < 3))
      cat("  *** cells with 1–2 species — consider merging levels ***\n")
    cat("\n")
  }
}
```


## Fourth corner fit
Fourth-corner test (Dray & Legendre 2008, Ecology 89:3400–3412). `modeltype=6`
combined permutation test; per-cell p-values, α = 0.05 (`fc_alpha`).
Run this chunk before `rlq_biplot` and `fourth_corner_plot`.

```{r fc_fit}
keep_awake()

fc_res <- fourthcorner(
  tabR               = R_mat,
  tabL               = L_wide,
  tabQ               = Q_mat,
  modeltype          = 6,
  p.adjust.method.D  = "none",
  p.adjust.method.G  = "none",
  nrepet             = 9999
)
print(fc_res)

nR <- length(fc_res$colnames.R)   # includes expanded habitat levels
nQ <- length(fc_res$colnames.Q)
fc_mat <- function(x) matrix(x, nrow = nR, ncol = nQ,
                             dimnames = list(fc_res$colnames.R, fc_res$colnames.Q))

## Per-cell (env variable or habitat level x trait level) results come from tabD2:
##  - continuous env x trait level: statistic "r" (signed correlation)
##  - habitat level x trait level:  statistic "N" (summed abundance in the cell; always
##    positive, so NOT a direction)
## Std.Obs = (observed - permutation mean) / permutation SD is signed and on the same
## scale for both: > 0 = positive association / over-represented, < 0 = the opposite.
## It is used for colour (direction) and |Std.Obs| for dot size.
## (Fixed 2026-10-26: habitat rows previously took p-values and dot sizes from tabG,
## which has one value per VARIABLE pair (5 x 4 = 20), recycled into the 7 x 14 cell
## grid, and coloured by N; continuous r values (+-0.11) all looked yellow on a +-26 scale.)
d2_mat   <- fc_mat(fc_res$tabD2$obs)                    # r or N (reference only)
ses_mat  <- fc_mat(fc_res$tabD2$expvar[, "Std.Obs"])    # signed standardised effect
pval_mat <- fc_mat(fc_res$tabD2$pvalue)                 # per-cell p (two-sided)
fc_alpha <- 0.05   # significance for tiles + RLQ trait arrows
cat(sprintf("cells with p <= %.2f: %d of %d\n", fc_alpha,
            sum(pval_mat <= fc_alpha), length(pval_mat)))

row_type <- fc_res$indexR[fc_res$assignR]   # 1 = continuous, 2 = categorical (habitat)
cat("R variable types (1=continuous, 2=categorical):\n")
print(data.frame(var = fc_res$colnames.R, type = row_type))

## variable-level tests (one per env variable x trait; F / Chi2), for the text
fc_var_tab <- data.frame(pair = fc_res$tabG$names, stat = fc_res$tabG$statnames,
                         obs = round(fc_res$tabG$obs, 3), p = fc_res$tabG$pvalue)
print(fc_var_tab)

allow_sleep()
```


## RLQ biplot and habitat ordination
RLQ site scores coloured by habitat with 75% data ellipses (`type = "norm"`
= data ellipse unaffected by sample size, unlike CI ellipses which inflate
with small n). Trait arrows filtered to fourth-corner significant levels
(p ≤ `fc_alpha` = 0.05 from fc_fit); all env variable arrows retained (only 4 total).

```{r rlq_biplot}
## ---- RLQ ordination ---------------------------------------------------------
afcL    <- dudi.coa(L_wide, scannf = FALSE, nf = 2)
acpR    <- dudi.hillsmith(R_mat, row.w = afcL$lw, scannf = FALSE, nf = 2)
acpQ    <- dudi.hillsmith(Q_mat, row.w = afcL$cw, scannf = FALSE, nf = 2)
rlq_res <- rlq(acpR, afcL, acpQ, scannf = FALSE, nf = 2)
summary(rlq_res)

tiff(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/RLQ_biplot_baseR.tiff"),
     width = 18, height = 15, units = "cm", res = 300)
plot(rlq_res)
dev.off()

## ---- Extract RLQ scores -----------------------------------------------------
rlq_sites <- as.data.frame(rlq_res$lR) %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
  rename(RLQ1 = 2, RLQ2 = 3) %>%
  ## habitat from R_mat (same samples as the RLQ, no NAs)
  mutate(habitat = factor(as.character(R_mat$habitat[match(sample_id, rownames(R_mat))]),
                          levels = names(hab_cols)))
stopifnot(!anyNA(rlq_sites$habitat))

rlq_env <- as.data.frame(rlq_res$l1) %>%
  rownames_to_column("var") %>%
  rename(RLQ1 = 2, RLQ2 = 3)

rlq_traits_all <- as.data.frame(rlq_res$c1) %>%
  rownames_to_column("trait") %>%
  rename(RLQ1 = 2, RLQ2 = 3)

## ---- Filter trait arrows to fourth-corner significant levels ----------------
## sig_fc_levels: trait levels where min p across env vars ≤ fc_alpha
sig_fc_levels <- fc_res$colnames.Q[apply(pval_mat, 2, min) <= fc_alpha]

rlq_traits_sig <- rlq_traits_all %>%
  filter(trait %in% sig_fc_levels) %>%
  mutate(label = sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", trait))  # strip trait-name prefix

## ---- Arrow scaling ----------------------------------------------------------
## Stretch arrows to ~75% of the site cloud radius
site_radius <- max(sqrt(rlq_sites$RLQ1^2 + rlq_sites$RLQ2^2), na.rm = TRUE)
env_radius  <- max(sqrt(rlq_env$RLQ1^2   + rlq_env$RLQ2^2),   na.rm = TRUE)
arr_mul     <- 0.75 * site_radius / env_radius

env_lbl_arr <- c(sst_mean      = "SST mean",
                 nitrate       = "Nitrate",
                 pp_range      = "PP range",
                 land_distance = "Dist. shore")

rlq_env_plot <- rlq_env %>%
  mutate(xend  = RLQ1 * arr_mul,  yend  = RLQ2 * arr_mul,
         lbl_x = RLQ1 * arr_mul * 1.18, lbl_y = RLQ2 * arr_mul * 1.18,
         ## habitat levels come out as "habitat.Coral" etc. -> label with the level name
         label = coalesce(unname(env_lbl_arr[var]), sub("^habitat\\.", "", var)))

## Scale trait arrows by the same factor
rlq_traits_plot <- rlq_traits_sig %>%
  mutate(xend  = RLQ1 * arr_mul,  yend  = RLQ2 * arr_mul,
         lbl_x = RLQ1 * arr_mul * 1.18, lbl_y = RLQ2 * arr_mul * 1.18)

## ---- Plot -------------------------------------------------------------------
## type = "norm" = data ellipse (spread of points, unaffected by n).
## level = 0.75 keeps ellipses compact; raise/lower to taste.
fig_rlq <- ggplot(rlq_sites, aes(RLQ1, RLQ2)) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(fill = habitat, colour = habitat),
               type = "norm", level = 0.75, geom = "polygon",
               alpha = 0.12, linewidth = 1.1, linetype = "solid") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = habitat, shape = habitat),
             size = 2.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  scale_shape_manual(values  = c(16, 17, 15), name = "Habitat") +
  ## Env arrows (blue)
  geom_segment(data = rlq_env_plot,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               colour = "#2166AC", linewidth = 0.9, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = rlq_env_plot,
            aes(x = lbl_x, y = lbl_y, label = label),
            colour = "#2166AC", size = 3.0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ## Trait arrows — fourth-corner significant only (red dashed)
  geom_segment(data = rlq_traits_plot,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               colour = "#C0392B", linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed",
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = rlq_traits_plot,
            aes(x = lbl_x, y = lbl_y, label = label),
            colour = "#C0392B", size = 2.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.border    = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8),
        legend.position = "right") +
  labs(x = "RLQ axis 1", y = "RLQ axis 2")

fig_rlq

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig_RLQ_biplot.tiff"),
```

## Fourth corner plot
Tile + dot plot: env variables on x-axis, trait categories on y-axis grouped
into trait facets. Tile shading = per-cell p ≤ 0.05; dot
colour = direction (standardised effect, blue = negative, red = positive); dot size =
strength (|standardised effect|).

```{r fourth_corner_plot}
## Axis labels: continuous env vars + habitat levels (expanded from factor)
## fc_res$colnames.R now includes "habitat.Coral", "habitat.Mangrove", etc.
env_lbl_cont <- c(sst_mean      = "SST (mean)",
                  nitrate       = "Nitrate",
                  pp_range      = "Prim. prod. (range)",
                  land_distance = "Dist. to shore")

## Build label for every expanded R variable:
## continuous vars get their nice name; habitat levels strip the "habitat." prefix
env_row_lbl <- setNames(
  ifelse(fc_res$colnames.R %in% names(env_lbl_cont),
         unname(env_lbl_cont[fc_res$colnames.R]),
         sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", fc_res$colnames.R)),
  fc_res$colnames.R
)

clean_level     <- sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", fc_res$colnames.Q)
trait_group     <- fc_res$varnames.Q[fc_res$assignQ]
trait_group_lbl <- c(zone                   = "Zone",
                     trophic_level          = "Trophic level",
                     size_class             = "Body size",
                     planktonic_larva       = "Planktonic larval",
                     mobility               = "Mobility")

to_long_fc <- function(mat, val) {
  as.data.frame(mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("env") %>%
    pivot_longer(-env, names_to = "trait_level", values_to = val)
}

## row_type_long: 1 = continuous, 2 = categorical (habitat); drives dot display.
row_type_vec <- setNames(row_type, fc_res$colnames.R)

fc_long <- to_long_fc(ses_mat, "SES") %>%
  left_join(to_long_fc(pval_mat, "p_value"), by = c("env", "trait_level")) %>%
  mutate(
    r_type      = unname(row_type_vec[env]),
    sig_tile    = if_else(p_value <= fc_alpha, "significant", "not significant"),
    ## colour = signed standardised effect, size = its magnitude (same for all rows)
    dot_size    = abs(SES),
    env_label   = unname(env_row_lbl[env]),
    level_clean = clean_level[match(trait_level, fc_res$colnames.Q)],
    trait_grp   = trait_group[match(trait_level, fc_res$colnames.Q)],
    trait_grp_f = factor(unname(trait_group_lbl[trait_grp]),
                         levels = unname(trait_group_lbl[fc_res$varnames.Q])),
    ## Habitat columns first (matching manyglm order), then continuous env vars
    env_f       = factor(env_label,
                         levels = unname(env_row_lbl[c(
                           names(row_type_vec)[row_type_vec == 2],
                           names(row_type_vec)[row_type_vec == 1]
                         )])),
    level_f     = factor(level_clean, levels = unique(clean_level))
  )


## Colour as Fig 4: yellow only in a narrow band around 0, so sign is obvious.
## Fixed limits +-3 standardised effect (values beyond are squished to the end colour).
ses_lim <- 3

fc_gg <- ggplot(fc_long, aes(env_f, level_f)) +
  facet_grid(trait_grp_f ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = sig_tile), colour = "grey50",
            width = 0.92, height = 0.92) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_sig, limits = names(col_sig), breaks = "significant",
                    labels = paste0("p \u2264 ", fc_alpha), name = NULL) +
  ## All rows (continuous + habitat): colour = signed standardised effect, size = |effect|
  geom_point(aes(colour = SES, size = dot_size)) +
  scale_colour_gradientn(
    name   = "Standardised\neffect",
    colors = pal_div,
    space  = "Lab",
    values = scales::rescale(c(-ses_lim * 1.1, -ses_lim / 9, 0, ses_lim / 9, ses_lim * 1.1)),
    limits = c(-ses_lim * 1.1, ses_lim * 1.1),
    breaks = c(-ses_lim, -ses_lim / 2, 0, ses_lim / 2, ses_lim),
    oob    = scales::squish
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Effect size", range = c(1, 7)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", angle = 0),
    strip.placement   = "outside",
    axis.text.x       = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y       = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.ticks        = element_blank(),
    panel.grid        = element_blank(),
    legend.position   = "right"
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)

fc_gg

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig6_fourth_corner.tiff"),
       fc_gg, width = 16, height = 20, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```




## Distance decay
Jaccard dissimilarity (presence/absence) vs. through-water geographic distance (km).

Run `through_water_dist` once to download bathymetry and compute the distance
matrix, then set that chunk to `eval=FALSE` for subsequent knits.

```{r through_water_dist, eval=FALSE}
## Downloads NOAA ETOPO1 bathymetry for the Red Sea and computes pairwise
## through-water distances between all sample sites. Land cells act as barriers
## so distances are routed through ocean only (unlike Haversine straight-line).
## Saves through_water_dist_km.csv; re-run only if sample locations change.
library(marmap)
library(terra)

## All sample locations before otu filtering
pts_all <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  distinct(sample_id, lon, lat)

## Download ETOPO1 at 1-arc-minute resolution (~1.85 km); cached as .csv in dir
bat <- marmap::getNOAA.bathy(
  lon1 = 31, lon2 = 45, lat1 = 11, lat2 = 31,
  resolution = 1,
  keep = TRUE,
  path = dir
)

## Convert to terra SpatRaster (marmap → raster → terra)
bat_rast <- terra::rast(marmap::as.raster(bat))

## Water mask: ocean (depth < 0) = 1; land (depth ≥ 0) = NA (barrier)
water_rast <- bat_rast
water_rast[bat_rast >= 0] <- NA
water_rast[!is.na(water_rast)] <- 1

## Dilate water mask by 1 cell (~1.85 km) so coastal sample points that fall
## just inside the land boundary of the raster are treated as water.
water_rast <- terra::focal(water_rast, w = 3, fun = "max", na.rm = TRUE,
                           na.policy = "omit")
water_rast[!is.na(water_rast)] <- 1

## Keep only the main connected water body (drops lagoons/ponds cut off by land at
## this resolution), so every pair of sites has a water route
wp <- terra::patches(water_rast, directions = 8)
main_patch <- as.integer(names(which.max(table(terra::values(wp, na.rm = TRUE)))))
water_rast[wp != main_patch] <- NA

## Snap sites whose cell is not in the main water body to the nearest water cell
## (coastal points can fall on land cells even after the dilation). Without this,
## those sites got NA distances and their pairs were silently dropped from Fig 7.
water_xy <- terra::xyFromCell(water_rast, which(!is.na(terra::values(water_rast))))
pts_all$cell <- terra::cellFromXY(water_rast, cbind(pts_all$lon, pts_all$lat))
pts_all$snap_km <- 0
for (i in which(is.na(terra::values(water_rast)[pts_all$cell]))) {
  near <- which(abs(water_xy[, 1] - pts_all$lon[i]) < 0.5 &
                abs(water_xy[, 2] - pts_all$lat[i]) < 0.5)
  dkm  <- terra::distance(cbind(pts_all$lon[i], pts_all$lat[i]), water_xy[near, , drop = FALSE],
                          lonlat = TRUE) / 1000
  k    <- near[which.min(dkm)]
  pts_all$cell[i]    <- terra::cellFromXY(water_rast, water_xy[k, , drop = FALSE])
  pts_all$snap_km[i] <- min(dkm)
}
cat("Sites snapped to water:", sum(pts_all$snap_km > 0), "; max shift",
    round(max(pts_all$snap_km), 1), "km\n")
n <- nrow(pts_all)

## Build symmetric distance matrix; gridDist routes through water only
tw_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, n, n,
                 dimnames = list(pts_all$sample_id, pts_all$sample_id))
diag(tw_mat) <- 0

for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  tmp <- water_rast
  tmp[pts_all$cell[i]] <- 2                       # mark focal site as target
  d <- terra::gridDist(tmp, target = 2) / 1000   # metres → km
  tw_mat[i, ] <- terra::values(d)[pts_all$cell]
}
tw_mat <- pmax(tw_mat, t(tw_mat))   # symmetric (differences are rounding only)
diag(tw_mat) <- 0
stopifnot(all(is.finite(tw_mat)))

write.csv(tw_mat, paste0(dir, "through_water_dist_km.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
cat("Saved:", n, "×", n, "through-water distance matrix\n")
```

## Fig 7 – distance decay plot
```{r dist_decay}
## ---- helper: dist object → data frame --------------------------------------
dist2df <- function(inDist) {
  A <- attr(inDist, "Size")
  B <- if (is.null(attr(inDist, "Labels"))) sequence(A) else attr(inDist, "Labels")
  if (isTRUE(attr(inDist, "Diag")))  attr(inDist, "Diag")  <- FALSE
  if (isTRUE(attr(inDist, "Upper"))) attr(inDist, "Upper") <- FALSE
  data.frame(
    row   = B[unlist(lapply(sequence(A)[-1], function(x) x:A))],
    col   = rep(B[-length(B)], (length(B) - 1):1),
    value = as.vector(inDist)
  )
}

## ---- presence/absence table (samples × taxa), same matrix as manyglm --------
otu_wide <- comm_pa

## no extra occurrence cut (only occurrence filter is in the filter script)

## ---- sample metadata (including habitat) ------------------------------------
sdat_dd <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  distinct(sample_id, lat, lon, habitat) %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(otu_wide)) %>%
  arrange(match(sample_id, rownames(otu_wide)))

## ---- Through-water distance (km) -------------------------------------------
## Load pre-computed matrix (run through_water_dist chunk once first)
tw_mat   <- as.matrix(read.csv(paste0(dir, "through_water_dist_km.csv"),
                               row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
tw_mat   <- tw_mat[sdat_dd$sample_id, sdat_dd$sample_id]
geo_dist <- as.dist(tw_mat)
attr(geo_dist, "Labels") <- sdat_dd$sample_id

## ---- Jaccard dissimilarity (presence/absence) --------------------------------
vg <- vegdist(otu_wide, method = "jaccard", binary = TRUE)

## ---- Build pairwise data frame with habitat labels --------------------------
pairs_df <- dist2df(geo_dist) %>%
  rename(sample1 = row, sample2 = col, km = value) %>%
  left_join(select(sdat_dd, sample_id, habitat), by = c("sample1" = "sample_id")) %>%
  rename(hab1 = habitat) %>%
  left_join(select(sdat_dd, sample_id, habitat), by = c("sample2" = "sample_id")) %>%
  rename(hab2 = habitat) %>%
  mutate(bc        = as.vector(vg),
         within_hab = if_else(hab1 == hab2, hab1, NA_character_),
         hab_pair   = if_else(hab1 == hab2, hab1, "Between habitats"))

## ---- Compute loess fits per habitat with 95% CI ----------------------------
loess_fits <- pairs_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(within_hab), is.finite(km)) %>%
  group_by(within_hab) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    fit    <- loess(bc ~ km, data = .x, span = 0.75)
    km_seq <- seq(min(.x$km), max(.x$km), length.out = 300)
    pred   <- predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(km = km_seq), se = TRUE)
    data.frame(km  = km_seq,
               fit = pred$fit,
               lwr = pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit,
               upr = pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(within_hab = factor(within_hab, levels = c("Coral", "Mangrove", "Seagrass"))) %>%
  arrange(within_hab)

## ---- Distance-decay plot by habitat -----------------------------------------
p_dd <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = filter(pairs_df, !is.na(within_hab), is.finite(km)),
             aes(km, bc, colour = within_hab), alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  ## Transparent coloured CI ribbon
  geom_ribbon(data = loess_fits,
              aes(x = km, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr, fill = within_hab),
              alpha = 0.22) +
  ## Thin lines on ribbon edges
  geom_line(data = loess_fits,
            aes(x = km, y = lwr, colour = within_hab),
            linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = loess_fits,
            aes(x = km, y = upr, colour = within_hab),
            linewidth = 0.25) +
  ## Solid loess line
  geom_line(data = loess_fits,
            aes(x = km, y = fit, colour = within_hab),
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  labs(x = "Through-water distance (km)",
       y = "Jaccard dissimilarity") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

p_dd

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig7_dist_decay.tiff"),
       p_dd, width = 14, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```

```{r mantel_diag, eval=FALSE}
## needs vg (Jaccard) and geo_dist (through-water km) from dist_decay
if (!exists("vg") || !exists("geo_dist")) stop("run the dist_decay chunk first")
mantel_corr <- mantel.correlog(vg, D.geo = geo_dist,
```
